FortiAuthenticator workspace

The FortiAuthenticator ADOM mirrors the unit's own menu and shows users, groups, tokens, certificates and RADIUS/TACACS+ clients live and read-only; changes go through the dry-run API console.

What is it?#

The FortiAuthenticator workspace is the SATOM ADOM for FortiAuthenticator identity servers. Its sidebar follows the menu the unit itself renders — System, Authentication, Fortinet SSO, Monitor, Certificate Management and Logging — and every section reads the selected unit live through its REST API. The section pages are read-only on purpose; changes are made on the pages of the unit's own menu (dry run first, read back and verified) or in the FortiAuthenticator API console, where writes are dry-run by default.

What does it do?#

  • Dashboard (/fac/) — the device picker, a Unit status card for the selected unit (Firmware, Serial, CPU, Memory, Disk and licence counters for Users, Groups, FSSO and SSO agents as used / max), and a card per menu group. Each section card shows its number of tabs, or no endpoint when nothing is bound. The subtitle reads N of 28 sections bound to live endpoints across 6 areas.
  • Section pages (/fac/m/<item>) — tabs for every API resource behind the section, read live. Lists show up to eight columns and a raw expander per row with the full object; single resources show as a key/value card.
  • Honest gaps — a section with no REST resource on the unit shows No endpoint bound. instead of an empty table.
  • Secret hiding — fields named password, secret, passwd, private_key or api_key are removed before a page is drawn, even if a firmware starts returning them.
  • API group in the sidebar — Registry & console.

Firmware and Device Backups are greyed out in this ADOM, and the firmware library and backup vault pages cannot be opened here by URL either: SATOM has no way to flash or back up a FortiAuthenticator with them. Certificate Manager (Operations › Automation) is greyed out too: SATOM manages certificates on FortiWeb and FortiADC only.

Requirements#

  • An appliance registered with kind fortiauthenticator. Its password field must hold the administrator's API key, not the login password. The key is issued on the unit by enabling Web service access on the administrator account.
  • If the unit uses a self-signed certificate, register it with certificate verification switched off (verify_ssl disabled), or every call fails before authenticating.
  • A selected unit (automatic when the ADOM holds exactly one).

Permissions#

Action Permission
Dashboard, section pages The legacy view gate, which any read permission grants (for example network.view)
Registry & console page (browse the catalog, run GET calls) registry.view
Write calls (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) in the API console registry.execute_write
Add, re-point, disable or restore registry endpoints registry.edit
Administrator group users.manage

Nobody can write from the section pages; there are no edit buttons there.

How to use#

Select a unit#

  1. Choose FortiAuthenticator in the product selector, or under ADOMs in the Global sidebar.
  2. Under FortiAuthenticator devices, click Select. The Unit status card appears for that unit.

Browse a section#

  1. Click a section, for example Authentication → User Management.
  2. The header shows the selected unit and host; the description explains what the section covers and which GUI panes have no API.
  3. Click a tab (for example FortiTokens). The card shows the label, the API path and the row count.
  4. Click raw at the end of a row to see the whole object as JSON.

Change something#

Section pages end with Read-only view. Writes go through the API console, where every request is explicit, dry-run by default and audited. Click API console in that sentence (or on the dashboard) and follow Product API pages.

The pages of the unit's own menu (the FortiAuthenticator group drawn from the GUI layouts measured on its build) also save: Save shows Review the change with the exact request, and Apply to <unit> sends it, needs a key that grants configuration writes, and reads the object back. The save shows Verified on the device, Not applied (the value the unit kept; the save fails) or Not verified.

When you rename an object SATOM caches by name — a user group, a RADIUS client or a RADIUS policy — its cached row moves to the new name. SATOM's copy then holds the object once, under its new name, and deleting it later leaves no row under the old name.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Appliance kind Must be fortiauthenticator Yes fortiauthenticator
Username The FortiAuthenticator administrator Yes satom-api
Password That administrator's API key Yes (the key emitted by the unit)
Verify SSL Switch off for self-signed certificates Depends off

Example#

🧪Example — Check FortiToken stock

  1. Select fac-01.
  2. On the dashboard, the Unit status card shows the licence counters.
  3. Open Authentication → User Management, tab FortiTokens, to list the tokens and their state.
  4. To assign a token, use the API console with a dry run first.

Result#

  • Section pages change nothing on the unit and are not audited.
  • Lists are read completely: SATOM follows the unit's pagination to the end, and if the walk stops early it shows the rows it got and the error.

Troubleshooting#

"401 unauthorized — FortiAuthenticator requires a per-user API key, not the login password."#

Possible causes — the appliance's password field holds the login password.

Solution 1. On the unit, enable Web service access for the administrator and copy the emitted key. 2. Store the key as the appliance's password under Administrator → Appliances.

Verification — the dashboard shows the Unit status card instead of The device refused the status read.

"403 forbidden — the API key authenticated but this resource is not permitted for …"#

Possible causes — the administrator's profile on the unit does not cover that resource.

Solution — widen the administrator's rights on the unit, or use an account that has them.

Verification — the tab lists rows.

Every call fails with a certificate error#

Possible causes — certificate verification is on and the unit presents a self-signed certificate.

Solution — switch off certificate verification on the appliance record, or install a certificate the SATOM server trusts.

Verification — the Unit status card loads.

"The device refused this read after N rows."#

Possible causes — the paginated read stopped part-way (timeout or device error).

Solution — reload the page; if it repeats, check the unit's load and the error shown under the message.

Verification — the row count matches the unit and no red box is shown.

"No endpoint bound."#

Possible causes — the unit exposes no REST resource for that pane on this firmware.

Solution — use the unit's GUI or CLI. If a newer firmware adds the resource, an administrator binds it on the registry page; the section then shows it without a code change.

Verification — the section shows tabs.

"Showing the first 500 of N rows."#

Possible causes — the resource holds more than 500 objects.

Solution — use the API console (a GET there is not truncated).

Verification — the console returns every row.

Advanced#

Advanced Transport

FortiAuthenticator speaks a plain REST API under /api/v1/ with HTTP Basic authentication (username + API key). Collections return meta and objects; singletons return a bare object. SATOM shows a single object as a key/value card when it has no resource_uri field. Section pages use a 20-second timeout; the dashboard status read uses 15 seconds.

Advanced Snapshot exclusions

The configuration harvest skips system_info, token_fortiguard_messages, token_ftm_licenses and cert_scep_requests, because their values change on an idle unit (CPU, quotas, the SCEP queue) and would look like configuration changes.

Advanced ADOM scoping

Entering any /fac/ or /fac/api/ page switches the browser tab to the FortiAuthenticator ADOM. Pages outside the FortiAuthenticator allow-list (including the firmware library and the backup vault) redirect to /fac/, and the appliance page of a FortiAuthenticator shows no View Backups button. Only appliances of kind fortiauthenticator are visible.
